releaseNotes: Resolved a two-month-old port-ledger inconsistency (docs/plans/attachments/2026-08-port-ledger.md): check-app-copy.ts and check-founder-copy.ts were dispositioned "port" by U8's original triage (structural/live-proof kernel survives, word-pattern prose-grading half dropped), but the split never executed -- both remained fully unchanged HYBRID validators. An llm-council review found the "port" disposition itself was the error: unlike validators that grade a self-attested report about a separate process (the disease "port"/"drop" target), the prose these two gates scan IS the shipped artifact itself -- COPY_DECK.md cells become literal app strings, founder-visible HTML/markdown is literally what a founder reads. Both rows revised port -> keep under this artifact-vs-report criterion, the same test that justified check-no-slop.ts's prior reinstatement -- closing the follow-up that row's reason column promised.

The council's chairman flagged that nobody had empirically re-verified the disputed word-pattern checks before trusting them (this repo's own standing rule: a gate is real only once it has been watched to fail). check-app-copy.ts's word-pattern half already had extensive fail-then-catch fixture coverage (verified live: 604/604 passing). check-founder-copy.ts's did not: the general banned-vocabulary rule (founder_copy.internal_vocabulary) had zero fixture coverage -- only a narrower technique-naming special case was tested. Verified live with a hand-injected banned term, then closed permanently with a new fixture case in validation/repository/fixtures/repo-gates.fixtures.ts.

No validator code changed -- both files keep their full original logic. Ledger summary/Total counts updated (port 27->25, keep 123->125) to stay in sync with verification/fixtures/catalog.fixtures.ts's mechanical ledger-completeness check.
